title: Junctions: Emerging, Turning & Priorities
whatItIs: Approaching, turning and emerging at junctions: who has priority, where to position, and the faults examiners record most.

keyFacts.text: At a 'Stop' sign and solid white line you MUST stop behind the line.
At broken white lines across the road you MUST give way to traffic on the main road.
You MUST NOT enter a yellow box until your exit is clear (except right turns held by oncoming traffic).

keyFacts: Give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you turn into or out of.
Turning right: just left of the middle of the road; don't cut the corner.

items.label: Stop line ('Stop' sign)
items.meaning: Stop behind the line; go only when safe.

items.label: Give way lines
items.meaning: Give way to traffic on the main road.

items.label: Yellow box junction
items.meaning: Don't enter until your exit is clear.

a.label: Right side to right side
points: Generally safer: clear view of traffic

b.label: Left side to left side
points: Turn in front of each other

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is turning left. A pedestrian is waiting to cross the side road. What should the pupil do?
onTheTest.why: Rules H2 and 170: give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road you are turning into. Beckoning them is a test fault.

onTheTest.question: A candidate looks, but misjudges a car that has to slow slightly. Safety isn't compromised. DT1 class?
onTheTest.why: DT1 11.05 gives this as a driving fault. Emerging into another vehicle's path without effective observation is serious.

traps: A car from the right signalling left may not turn: wait and make sure.
Waiting when it's safe to go is a fault too (undue hesitation).
Lights out of order? Treat it as an unmarked junction: nobody has priority.
